subject: english
question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To flog a dead horse'

options.text: Beat an animal to carry goods
Work hard and win a prize

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Waste time on lost cause.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To flog a dead horse"** means to waste time and effort on something that has no chance of succeeding or is already a lost cause. (खोए हुए कारण पर समय बर्बाद करना)

 
 
• **Example: **Trying to convince him to change his mind is like flogging a dead horse; he’s already made his decision.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom suggests putting effort into something that has no hope of yielding results.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Beat an animal to carry goods** (जानवर को सामान ले जाने के लिए मारना): This option refers to physically beating an animal to make it work, which is unrelated to the idiom.
 
 
• **Example:** It is cruel to beat animals to carry heavy loads.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Complain loudly and cry** (जोर से शिकायत करना और रोना): This option refers to expressing dissatisfaction loudly, which does not align with the meaning of the idiom.
 
 
• **Example:** She began to complain loudly when her order was delayed.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Work hard and win a prize** (कड़ी मेहनत करना और पुरस्कार जीतना): This option emphasizes effort and success, which is the opposite of the idiom’s meaning.
 
 
• **Example:** He worked hard and won the first prize in the competition.
 
 

33:Tc58,
The correct answer is **Option 1**.
